title: Americans Spend 67 Days a Year Feeling 'Half Present'
paragraphs: You're trying to work or study, but you can't focus. You're tired, or just not interested, or thinking about something else — like all the things you still have to do today, or that argument you had with your best friend yesterday.
How many days a year would you say you feel like this?

If you ask the average American, they would say it's 67 days. That's according to a survey of 2,000 US adults by Talker Research. Americans say they spend an average of 5.6 days per month feeling "half present" — that's more than one day a week.

For the survey, feeling "half present" was defined as not giving your full attention to people or tasks, thinking about other things instead of what you're doing, or feeling too tired to be fully engaged in what's happening around you.
And young people aged 18 to 29 have almost twice as many "half present" days as those aged 62 to 80. Young people have 84 half present days a year, compared to 46 for older people.
When asked what keeps them from being fully present, the top answer — named by 39% of participants — was not getting enough sleep.
After that, the reasons varied by age.

Participants under 30 said phone notifications and relationship problems were the next biggest things keeping them from feeling fully present. For those aged 30 to 45, it was burnout and headaches. For everyone older, it was money problems.

And one big reason people don't get enough sleep is getting sick. Fifty-five percent of participants said they get five hours of sleep or less when they have a cold or the flu — almost double the 28% who get that little sleep when they're healthy.
The survey was done for Mucinex Recharge, a nighttime cold and flu medicine.
